leamington spa.s1_head: Charity and volunteer kit in Leamington Spa
s1loc: Royal Leamington Spa anchors a busy charity scene led by Warwick District Foodbank, the Trussell Trust member that grew out of the 2013 Warwick and Leamington effort and merged with Kenilworth in 2017. The Myton Hospices run shops on Bedford Street and Warwick Street, while Helping Hands on Oxford Street supports people who are homeless or rebuilding after crisis. The Lillington Community Pantry and the SJB Food Kitchen add to the network, with the big food-redistribution charities moving surplus into projects right across the district.

The sector here runs at every size. National and regional charities keep shops and central buying lines along The Parade and Bath Street, while tiny volunteer-run projects work on a shoestring from church halls in Sydenham, Lillington and Brunswick. The Brunswick Hub runs a community food project and the Leamington and Warwick Gurdwara feeds anyone who calls. WCAVA links volunteers to causes across Warwick District. We are glad to serve the national charity and the one-room foodbank alike, with trade accounts and direct online ordering, no minimum.

Beyond the foodbanks, the Myton Hospices draw hundreds of shop volunteers across Coventry and Warwickshire, and the SYDNI Centre serves the multicultural Sydenham estate with community activity. The LWS Night Shelter coordinates winter beds with local supporters, Life Community Church runs CAP debt help and a foodbank, and charity-shop rails line Regent Street and Warwick Street. Mutual-aid groups in Whitnash and Old Town keep neighbours fed and connected, and volunteer drivers ferry parcels out to households who cannot reach a centre themselves.

kidderminster.s1_head: Charity and volunteer kit in Kidderminster
s1loc: Kidderminster sits at the heart of the Wyre Forest district, where Kidderminster Foodbank, a Trussell Trust member, relieves financial hardship with emergency food, toiletries and household items. Franche Community Church runs the Wyre Forest Food Bank delivery service covering Kidderminster, Stourport and Bewdley, working from Baxter Church and other sites. KEMP Hospice has cared for the district for more than fifty-five years, and the big food-redistribution networks keep surplus flowing into the projects that hand it on to families in crisis.

The sector runs at every size here. KEMP Hospice operates six shops, a furniture store and a donation centre on Lisle Avenue with central buying behind them, while small volunteer-run foodbanks work on a shoestring from churches in Franche, Spennells and Horsefair. National charity rails sit along Vicar Street and the Swan Centre, and tiny pantries and mutual-aid groups serve estates across the district. We are glad to serve the national charity and the one-room foodbank alike, with trade accounts and direct online ordering, no minimum.

Wider Wyre Forest support reaches well beyond the foodbanks. KEMP Hospice gives end-of-life care, counselling and emotional support free of charge, kept going by volunteers across its Kidderminster, Stourport and Bewdley shops. Community groups listed in the Wyre Forest Community Directory run lunch clubs and befriending, charity shops dot Worcester Street and Coventry Street, and volunteer drivers carry parcels out to Habberley and Comberton. New starts projects and church-run larders keep neighbours fed, and local mutual-aid networks step in when households fall through the gaps.

weymouth.s1_head: Charity and volunteer kit in Weymouth
s1loc: Weymouth Foodbank, started by Lily and Bob Mockett in 2012 and working in partnership with local churches, runs from Weymouth Baptist Church with satellite sites at St Francis Church in Littlemoor and Westham Methodist Church. Its hub on Cambridge Road in the Granby Industrial Estate hands out nutritionally balanced emergency food to people referred in need. Weldmar Hospicecare anchors end-of-life care across the area, and the big food-redistribution networks and FareShare pop-up larders push surplus into projects right across Dorset.

The sector runs at every size here. Weldmar Hospicecare keeps shops on St Thomas Street, Great George Street, Lodmoor and a Weymouth outlet, with central buying and collection rounds behind them, while small volunteer-run foodbanks work on a shoestring from church halls in Westham, Wyke Regis and Portland. National charity rails line St Mary Street and the town-centre precinct, and tiny pantries serve estates across the borough. We are glad to serve the national charity and the one-room foodbank alike, with trade accounts and direct online ordering, no minimum.

Across Weymouth and Portland the network runs deep. Weldmar Hospicecare collects donations and runs a Wyke Regis shop and a Portland store in Easton Square, all kept open by volunteers serving at the till and sorting stock. Help and Kindness lists scores of community groups and volunteering roles within ten miles, the Dorset Community Response team coordinates support, and charity shops cluster along St Thomas Street. Mutual-aid groups in Littlemoor and Melcombe Regis keep neighbours fed, and volunteer drivers carry parcels out to households who cannot reach a centre.

canterbury.s1_head: Charity and volunteer kit in Canterbury
s1loc: Canterbury Food Bank provides emergency three-day food parcels to families in crisis across Canterbury, Whitstable, Herne Bay and surrounding villages, with volunteer drivers running delivery rounds across the district. Catching Lives, an independent charity off the city centre, supports people who are homeless or insecurely housed across Canterbury and East Kent, staying open seven days a week. Pilgrims Hospices cares for the dying across east Kent, and FareShare in Kent and the big food-redistribution networks move surplus into the projects that pass it on.

The sector runs at every size here. Pilgrims Hospices, Porchlight and Demelza keep shops with central buying lines along St George's Street and the high street, while small volunteer-run foodbanks and pantries work on a shoestring from church halls in Wincheap, St Stephen's and Thanington. Porchlight, based on New Town Street, supports people facing homelessness and poverty across Kent. We are glad to serve the national charity and the one-room foodbank alike, with trade accounts and direct online ordering, no minimum.

Beyond the foodbanks the city carries a deep charity tradition. Pilgrims Hospices runs shops and recruits volunteers, including at Horsebridge Books in nearby Whitstable, while Catching Lives leans on volunteers to keep its day centre, showers and laundry running. Demelza children's hospice has a Canterbury shop always seeking weekend helpers, and charity rails fill Wincheap and Northgate. Mutual-aid groups around St Stephen's and Wincheap keep neighbours connected, and the council points new community groups to local volunteer-support organisations and grant help.

barry.s1_head: Charity and volunteer kit in Barry
s1loc: Vale Foodbank opened in Barry in September 2011 and now runs eight centres across the Vale of Glamorgan, a project founded by local churches working to stop hunger. FareShare Cymru, founded in 2010 and based in Cardiff, rescues surplus food and redistributes it to charities and community groups right across Wales, including the Vale. Marie Curie runs a charity shop on Holton Road and cares for terminally ill people through its Cardiff and the Vale hospice, with the big food-redistribution networks feeding projects across town.

The sector runs at every size here. National and regional charities keep shops and central buying lines along Holton Road and the town centre, while small volunteer-run foodbanks and pantries work on a shoestring from church and community halls in Cadoxton, Gibbonsdown and Buttrills. Glamorgan Voluntary Services, an independent charity, supports volunteers and community organisations across the Vale. We are glad to serve the national charity and the one-room foodbank alike, with trade accounts and direct online ordering, no minimum.

Across Barry the voluntary network runs deep. Marie Curie keeps its Holton Road shop open with local volunteers, and Glamorgan Voluntary Services links residents to causes across the Vale through its volunteer brokerage. Dementia-friendly groups support older neighbours, infoengine lists scores of community services for the county, and charity rails line Holton Road and Broad Street. Mutual-aid groups around Cadoxton and the Waterfront keep neighbours fed and connected, and volunteer drivers carry parcels out to households who cannot reach a Vale Foodbank centre.

hamilton.s1_head: Charity and volunteer kit in Hamilton
s1loc: Hamilton District Foodbank, a project founded by local churches and community groups, works to stop hunger across the town and is kept running by volunteers at its distribution sites. BASICS Food Bank Lanarkshire, a Christian charity, hands out food parcels and toiletries from outlets including Motherwell, Wishaw, Airdrie and Viewpark. St Andrew's Hospice cares for adults, children and families with life-limiting illness, and the big food-redistribution networks and FareShare move surplus into projects right across Lanarkshire.

The sector runs at every size here. St Andrew's Hospice runs shops with central buying across North and South Lanarkshire, including a Quarry Street shop in Hamilton, while small volunteer-run foodbanks and pantries work on a shoestring from church halls in Blantyre, Burnbank and Larkhall. Voluntary Action South Lanarkshire links volunteers to causes across the area. We are glad to serve the national charity and the one-room foodbank alike, with trade accounts and direct online ordering, no minimum.

Across Hamilton the voluntary effort runs deep. St Andrew's Hospice counts hundreds of volunteers giving around a hundred thousand hours a year across its Lanarkshire shops, alongside bereavement counselling and wellbeing services. Larkhall and District Foodbank keeps its own wish list filled by neighbours, charity rails line Quarry Street and the Regent Centre, and mutual-aid groups around Blantyre and Earnock keep neighbours fed. Volunteer drivers carry parcels out to households who cannot reach a distribution point, and church larders step in across the district.

folkestone.s1_head: Charity and volunteer kit in Folkestone
s1loc: The Rainbow Centre in Folkestone offers homeless support, a winter shelter and the Shepway Foodbank, which provides three days of nutritionally balanced emergency food to people referred in crisis across the Folkestone and Hythe district. The Folkestone Pantry lets members buy food at a low weekly cost plus free essentials, and the Salvation Army adds further support. Pilgrims Hospices cares for the dying across east Kent, and the big food-redistribution networks keep surplus flowing into projects right across the district.

The sector runs at every size here. Pilgrims Hospices keeps a general shop on Sandgate Road and a Folkestone furniture shop with central buying behind them, while small volunteer-run foodbanks and pantries work on a shoestring from church halls in Cheriton, Sandgate and the Harbour ward. The council's district food network links the social supermarkets and pantries across the area. We are glad to serve the national charity and the one-room foodbank alike, with trade accounts and direct online ordering, no minimum.

Across Folkestone the voluntary network runs deep. The Rainbow Centre pairs its foodbank with money advice and family-contact support, run largely by community volunteers, while Pilgrims Hospices shop teams have clocked up a century of combined service. The Kent Community Pantry recruits helpers, charity rails line Sandgate Road and the Old High Street, and mutual-aid groups around Cheriton and Morehall keep neighbours fed. Volunteer drivers carry parcels out to households who cannot reach a centre, and church-run larders step in across the district.
